rationale: A wins because it knows where the story ends and where the unsupported temptation begins. "Resale and repair stop being a pilot: REI puts trade-in and gear repair in all 180+ stores" is a clean, grounded operational angle with a real peg; B's "As outdoor gear floods secondhand apps" starts by inventing a market condition the update did not give it. B has usable instincts, but it keeps turning proof gaps into headlines, which is how founders get walked into bad reporter calls.
gaps_in_A: "The prevailing belief: resale and repair cannibalize new-product sales" is a useful tension, but it is not in the supplied update. A mostly handles the hole honestly, but the angle still needs outside evidence before it leads.

"repair counter in every store" over-specifies the member experience. The update says repairs are available at 180+ stores; it does not say every store has a visible counter or the same staffing model.
gaps_in_B: "public retailers can't easily replicate" is too strong for the facts. The update says REI is a co-op; it does not prove public retailers cannot copy the model.
"As outdoor gear floods secondhand apps" is invented scenery. No secondhand-app volume, market flood, or competitive shift appears in the update.
"Both announcements — the record dividend and the nationwide trade-in expansion — are live this week" invents timing. The dividend happened this year; the update does not say it landed this week.

"REI's repair expansion adds skilled technician work at stores already navigating union campaigns" may be a real labor story, but it is a hazardous story for REI to pitch. This belongs in defensive prep unless the company has hard store-level facts and an answer on pay/classification.
